title: Why you can't tickle yourself
note: Pipeline test episode. Topic is a placeholder until the reference format is measured.

lines.text: Every time you move, your brain sends a copy of that command to a spot called the cerebellum.
It uses that copy to predict what you're about to feel.
And anything it predicts, it turns down.
That's why someone else can make you squirm,
but your own fingers barely register.
Scientists tested this with a robot.
People moved a handle, and the robot tickled them.
With no delay, it barely tickled.
But add a fraction of a second of lag, and the tickle started coming back.
Your brain isn't ignoring you. It just saw you coming.
